scope.geography: United States; San Jose and greater San Francisco Bay Area prioritized first, Cleveland/Ohio second, then nationwide
scope.selection_rule: Current actionable roles only; Bay Area roles receive a geographic preference when fit is comparable; stale or expired postings excluded.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Scholar — IBD, Microbiome and Multi-Omics
jobs.job_description: Human-focused IBD research spanning Crohn's disease, microbiome/metabolome studies, scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics and translational intervention studies.
jobs.why_good_match: Exceptionally strong biological match in the preferred Bay Area: Crohn's disease, human studies, microbiome, scRNA-seq and multi-omics all overlap current work while adding clinical translational depth and Stanford's ecosystem.
likely_gaps: NIH training-grant funding means U.S. citizens/permanent residents are preferred
jobs.tailor: Lead with the Crohn's host-microbiome chip, patient-derived epithelium, scRNA-seq and shotgun/HUMAnN analysis; pitch the next step as connecting controlled mechanistic models to human longitudinal multi-omics.
jobs.immediate_action: Contact Dr. Sinha now. Because returning to San Jose is a real preference, this should move to the top of the academic application queue if eligibility fits.

jobs.title: Associate Staff Scientist (Intestinal Organoids)
jobs.job_description: Develop, optimize and characterize intestinal organoid platforms for IBD, drug discovery, predictive toxicology and regenerative applications.
key_must_have_requirements: Independent experimental design and scientific communication
jobs.why_good_match: Still the strongest Ohio technical match: intestinal organoids, IBD, tissue engineering and advanced human-model development map directly to current expertise.
likely_gaps: iPSC-derived intestinal organoid depth relative to adult patient-derived organoids
jobs.tailor: Lead with patient-derived intestinal organoids and Crohn's chips, followed by scRNA-seq, imaging and engineering; explicitly show how adult-stem-cell expertise transfers to iPSC systems.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply now, but compare scientific ownership and promotion path directly against Stanford before choosing based on topic fit alone.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Associate — Gastrointestinal Host Immune-Microbiome Organ-on-Chip
jobs.job_description: Build GI host-immune-microbiome models using organoid engineering, organ-on-chip, microfluidics and microbiome science for Crohn's disease, UC and related disorders.
jobs.why_good_match: Near-exact scientific overlap, with the immune compartment providing the clearest new capability beyond current epithelial-microbiome work.
likely_gaps: Risk of repeating too much of the PhD technical portfolio
jobs.tailor: Frame immune integration as the missing mechanistic layer and emphasize susceptibility-exposure Crohn's work, patient-derived models and microbiota co-culture.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply, but require a clear independent hypothesis and first-author path before ranking it above Stanford or a more differentiating engineering postdoc.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow – NHP Immunology and Organ Chips

salary.note: Not listed on current Wyss page.

jobs.posting_status: Official Wyss academic opening remains live
jobs.job_description: Use Organ Chips, spatial omics and functional assays to compare adaptive immunity and radiation toxicity across human and non-human-primate systems, with regulatory and pharma interaction.
jobs.why_good_match: Radiation toxicity plus Organ Chips remains uniquely aligned with radiation-on-chip experience while adding spatial omics, immunology and regulatory exposure.
jobs.tailor: Open with radiation-on-chip, ROS/DNA-damage/barrier assays and Organ-Chip engineering; use scRNA-seq as evidence of omics adaptability.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply while the official opening remains live.

jobs.title: Assistant Project Scientist — 3D Bioprinters, Bioreactors and AI for Bioprinting
jobs.term: Project Scientist appointment; duration depends on project timeline and funding
jobs.posting_status: Official recruitment open; next review October 21, 2026
jobs.job_description: Develop DLP-based 3D bioprinters, bioreactors, hardware/software and machine-learning methods for bioprinting optimization.
jobs.why_good_match: High-upside engineering expansion that could convert current microfabrication, 3D printing and fluidic hardware work into a much deeper biofabrication platform identity.
jobs.tailor: Make the engineering portfolio central: porous PDMS membranes, multiplex fluidics, pumps/actuators, 3D printing and iterative device troubleshooting; acknowledge the DLP/ML gap directly.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply as a stretch before the October 21 review if platform engineering is a deliberate post-PhD expansion goal.
